permit_authority.value: City of Little Rock Building Codes Division
permit_authority.notes: Part of the Planning and Development department; handles building, plumbing, mechanical, and electrical permitting, plan review, and inspections citywide, via six working sections.

interconnection_url.notes: Confirmed directly from Entergy Arkansas's own Arkansas Public Service Commission-filed tariff (Rate Schedule No. 71, Non-Legacy Net-Metering Service, effective 3/1/24 with Attachment A revised 3/2/26): excess generation is credited at the Company's Avoided Cost — NOT full retail rate. The exact published Avoided Cost rate: $0.0259/kWh (March 2024-February 2025), $0.0247/kWh (March 2025-February 2026), $0.0334/kWh (March 2026-February 2027), redetermined annually based on the prior calendar year's average Locational Marginal Price in the Company's MISO load zone. 'Non-Legacy' applies to customers who submitted an SIA, Facilities Agreement, or complaint after September 30, 2024; customers with interconnection documents in place by that date retain 'legacy' status under the prior (more favorable) net-metering structure instead.

battery_programs.notes: No confirmed financial battery storage incentive program was found in Entergy Arkansas's own net metering page or tariff, or on the City's own permitting pages, this session.

required_documents.notes: The utility-side document checklist is precisely confirmed from Entergy Arkansas's own PSC-filed tariff form. No Little Rock-specific solar PV permit checklist was found this session — the City's general building/electrical permit requirements are recorded from its own Building Codes Division page instead.

value: The customer shall not commence Parallel Operation of the Net-Metering Facility until it has been inspected and approved by Entergy Arkansas

The Standard Interconnection Agreement's own Certification section requires sign-off from the local Building/Electrical Code inspector (of the applicable City/County) confirming the system complies with the National Electrical Code, IEEE standards, the National Electrical Safety Code, and UL listing requirements, or a copy of the final inspection certificate may be attached in lieu of signature

value.notes: Per Entergy Arkansas's own PSC-filed tariff: after a customer submits a Standard Interconnection Agreement (required at least 30 days before the intended interconnection date), the Company reviews the facility plans and provides written results within 30 calendar days; the same 30-calendar-day review window applies to the optional Preliminary Interconnection Site Review Request. No City of Little Rock-specific building/electrical permit review timeline was independently confirmed from a primary source this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Non-Legacy Net-Metering Service (Arkansas Public Service Commission Rate Schedule No. 71) — for residential customers, generating capacity is capped at the lesser of 25kW or the capacity representing the customer's highest residential usage in the previous 12 months.
other_conditions: Net-Metering customers may not simultaneously take service under any other alternative-source-generation, co-generation, or interruptible-service tariff.
A Net-Metering Facility may not be modified or changed to generate more electricity than needed to offset the customer's own requirements.

Customers whose interconnection documents (SIA, Facilities Agreement, or complaint) were in place by September 30, 2024 retain 'legacy' status under the prior net-metering credit structure instead of this Non-Legacy avoided-cost rate.
